principles: Reuse existing lifecycle truth sources instead of duplicating gates.
Keep local Non-authority closure separate from Authority Server proof.
Make TEST PASS != DONE mechanically visible to agents.
Prefer narrow read-only observability over lifecycle mutation.
drivers: Existing done-oracle already centralizes DONE pre-check rows.
Operators need a stable machine-readable runbook, not prose-only hints.

options.name: A: Add read-only done_closure handler backed by buildDoneChecklist
pros: Provides stable JSON/text contract without weakening DONE gate
Reuses existing oracle rows and can include explicit authorityServerPath fields
Keeps session_brief behavior intact while adding a focused command
cons: Adds a new CLI surface and requires command/process-fact registration

options.name: B: Only expand session_brief and next wording
cons: Does not provide a stable machine-readable runbook contract
Can continue to be read as advisory prose rather than an executable closure checklist

options.name: C: Automate delivery-check and summary generation
cons: Would forge or weaken reviewer/user-value gates
Optimizes arbitrarily beyond the real correctness issue

chosen: A: Add read-only done_closure handler backed by buildDoneChecklist
rationale: Option A directly addresses the correctness issue with the smallest safe mechanical capability: a read-only runbook backed by the existing DONE oracle, with explicit Non-authority and Authority separation.

preMortem.scenario: The new command duplicates DONE gate predicates and drifts from story_advance DONE.
preMortem.trigger: A handler rebuilds branch, delivery, summary, or evidence rules by hand.
preMortem.consequence: Agents receive a green runbook while DONE gate still blocks, recreating the original confusion.
preMortem.mitigation: Call buildDoneChecklist and test same-source behavior through flow-stability/done-preflight coverage.

preMortem.scenario: Local runbook output is mistaken for Authority completion.
preMortem.trigger: Output includes authority-like success wording without receipt verification fields.
preMortem.consequence: Lattice overclaims receiptVerified or fullAuthorityDone from local CLI evidence.
preMortem.mitigation: Return authorityServerPath with receiptVerified=false and mayClaimAuthorityDone=false unless verified receipt refs exist.

preMortem.scenario: The assistant becomes mutating closure automation.
preMortem.trigger: Implementation writes delivery-check, summary, or advances DONE from done_closure.
preMortem.consequence: Reviewer signatures and user-value closure can be forged by the main agent.
preMortem.mitigation: Classify command as read-only lifecycle observability and add tests asserting no lifecycle artifacts are written.

preMortem.scenario: Implementation scope expands into Authority Server redesign.
preMortem.trigger: Developer tries to solve Authority mode inside this local runbook story.
preMortem.consequence: Large risky changes obscure the TEST PASS != DONE fix.
preMortem.mitigation: Keep Authority mode to guidance/projection only and defer receipt-backed server changes to dedicated stories.
